edits.old: Synced files carry user identity. A .NET maintainer explained that different users need separate Realm files and that copying another user's prefilled synced file does not remove its user association. The Java SyncConfiguration.Builder also places synced files under user-specific paths derived from the Realm URI by default. (high confidence)
edits.new: Synced files carry user identity. A .NET maintainer explained that each user needs their own Realm file and that a prefilled synced database is associated with a certain user. The Realm Object Server-era Java SyncConfiguration.Builder places synced files by default under a user-ID-specific path derived from the Realm URI. Sources: https://github.com/realm/realm-dotnet/issues/3205 ; https://realm.netlify.app/docs/java/latest/api/io/realm/syncconfiguration.builder

edits.rationale: The legacy Realm Java SyncConfiguration.Builder offers disableSSLVerification() and says not to use it in production. The legacy Realm Swift SyncConfiguration (3.4.0) has enableSSLValidation true by default and says never to disable it in production. The claim's 'or' wording matches this: Swift is on by default, and Java provides an explicit disabling option.
